subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway and embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, and hooks?
rationale: This would be a user-trusted security and product guarantee, and current source has multiple execution surfaces that a narrow process-global adapter flag would not safely cover.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Defer to broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this blocked until the Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode design chooses the shared vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Keep only scoped dry-runs
options.body: Decline a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing, and continue improving command-specific preview paths instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history on the adapter/tool execution boundary and product/security direction for this issue.
